options.text: It is a working Voltaic cell if the two different metal electrodes and the lemon juice electrolyte produce a current that lights the LED.
It is a working Voltaic cell even if both strips are made of the same metal.
It is a working Voltaic cell because the LED housing is present, even if the LED stays dark.
It cannot be a Voltaic cell because lemon juice cannot act as an electrolyte.

stem:
The diagram shows Simran's lemon setup: a copper strip and an iron strip pushed into a lemon, with wires joining the strips to an LED.

Which claim correctly judges whether this is a working Voltaic cell?

teacher.key_rationale: A working Voltaic cell needs two electrodes of different metals and an electrolyte such as lemon juice; a glowing LED shows current. Same-metal strips omit a required condition; a dark LED with only a housing present is not evidence of a working cell; lemon juice can serve as the electrolyte.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source circuit symbols into a lemon Voltaic cell with copper and iron electrodes and an LED.
